parallel.requirements: Implemented the six progressive RV32IM labs and recognized Lab6 as Tomasulo with reservation stations, CDB, RAT, functional units, and official iverilog testing obligations.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept Lab1 and final commit/patch duties, then spawned a five-item AgentSwarm to verify and fix labs 2 through 6 independently.
parallel.implementation: The final implementation covered most modules and local simulations, but Lab6 FU_jump retained a dependency on MUX2T1_32 that was not self-contained for the official FU-only compile.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After the swarm returned PASS reports, the parent cleaned generated binaries, staged each lab, wrote requirement_patches/labN.diff, and committed six per-lab changes.
parallel.verification: Verification relied on child local testbenches and broad `core/*.v common/*.v` compiles; the official run later showed 20 passed and one Lab6 FU compile failure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The unresolved issue at closure was Lab6 FU import closure: official compilation of FU_ALU, FU_jump, ImmGen, and selected common files lacked MUX2T1_32.

serial.requirements: Worked from the same six-lab prompt and preserved the Lab6 Tomasulo/FU obligations, including functional unit behavior and test-compatible module interfaces.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one non-delegated main trajectory, carrying implementation, verification, and final acceptance state in the same context across rounds.
serial.implementation: Implemented and revised the Lab6 core and functional units in the main trajectory, including direct inspection of RV32core, CtrlUnit, ROM/RAM, and Lab3 memory inputs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Sequential edits and checks remained in one workspace, with final output accepted by the official harness without a child handoff boundary.
serial.verification: The official post-test shows all 21 tests passed, including the Lab6 FU module compile that failed in the parallel run.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished requirement remained; status.json marks the completed evaluation solution_passed true.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the six-lab RV32IM implementation task and the Lab6 Tomasulo/FU obligations, then treated all six as covered at closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run worked from the same prompt and kept the six labs, including Lab6 FU and Tomasulo requirements, in one sequential context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both saw the task scope, but only the serial solution satisfied the official Lab6 FU standalone compile requirement; the parallel path treated broader local simulation as enough.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent verified Lab1 locally and delegated labs 2 through 6 to five child agents, each scoped to one lab, then resumed final commits itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used one main trajectory with no delegation and iterated through the same lab work sequentially.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification ownership crossed a parent-child boundary for Lab6, while serial kept discovery, implementation, and acceptance in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The Lab6 child was asked to compile lab sources plus testbenches, but the brief did not state the official FU-only source list or require dependency self-containment.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run inspected Lab6 source structure directly and compared Lab6 Lab3 memory files against the Lab3 originals before continuing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The missing interface contract exists only in the parallel handoff: the child validated against `common/*.v`, which hid a dependency absent from the official FU compile list.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel Lab6 implementation left `FU_jump.v` dependent on `MUX2T1_32`, which is available in the full common wildcard build but not in the official FU source subset.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial implementation path produced Lab6 FU files that compiled under the official source subset.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementation difference is import closure: parallel required an extra module outside the official FU source list, while serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The Lab6 child returned a completed PASS handoff and the parent consumed the aggregate swarm result before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt did not depend on child result retrieval; the main trajectory carried its own observations forward.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No child result was lost, but the parallel lifecycle made the parent rely on a child acceptance summary that omitted the official import-closure check.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent staged and committed the per-lab work after receiving child reports, with no observed write collision or overwrite causing the failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run made sequential edits and checks in one workspace; no parallel shared-state conflict is present in the control.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The difference is not a concurrent write race; it is that parallel integration accepted a Lab6 file dependency that was compatible with wildcard simulation but not the official standalone FU build.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel Lab6 verification compiled and simulated with `core/*.v common/*.v`, then reported PASS; official acceptance later failed the narrower Lab6 FU compile.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial official acceptance passed all 21 tests, including the Lab6 FU compile.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decisive verification gap is evaluator alignment: the parallel child test masked a missing dependency, while serial delivered an implementation accepted by the official compile target.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent closed after the swarm reports and six per-lab commits, with no visible recheck of the official FU-only Lab6 target.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also hit process time limits across rounds, but its final official evaluation completed and passed all tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Budget pressure is not the retained pattern; the material closure difference is that parallel closed on delegated local verification, while serial closure left a grader-compatible Lab6 FU dependency set.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This is a serial_only_pass pair. The parallel run did substantial implementation and local verification, but its Lab6 verifier used a broad compile recipe that included every common module. That masked the fact that FU_jump.v required MUX2T1_32 even though the official Lab6 FU compile intentionally supplied only add_32.v, cmp_32.v, REG32.v, FU_ALU.v, FU_jump.v, and ImmGen.v. The parent accepted the child PASS and finalized, so the official evaluator failed on Unknown module type MUX2T1_32. The serial run kept Lab6 source inspection and verification in one actor and the official Lab6 FU compile passed.
parallel_contributors: Lab6 verification was delegated without an explicit official FU-only source-list/import-closure contract.
The Lab6 child compiled with `core/*.v common/*.v`, so the missing standalone dependency did not surface before the parent accepted the PASS handoff.
serial_contributors: The serial main trajectory inspected Lab6 sources and memory dependencies directly rather than accepting a child verifier summary.
The serial final artifact passed the official Lab6 FU compile and the complete 21-test official suite.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel `FU_jump.v` depended on `MUX2T1_32` outside the official FU source list; serial did not leave that dependency unresolved for the official compile target.
evaluator_effects: The status.json outcome resolver provides solution_passed booleans but no current passed/total/rate metrics, so the review records null counts even though post-test panes display 20/21 and 21/21.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
